job.title: Who Was Polycarp? The 86-Year-Old Who Chose the Fire
job.description:
He was 86 years old. The Roman governor gave him one way out of the stadium alive: curse Christ. This is what Polycarp said back, and what it cost him.

Polycarp of Smyrna was taught by the apostle John. Around AD 155 the police came for him at a farmhouse outside the city. He fed the men who arrested him, asked for an hour to pray, and rode to the stadium on a donkey. In front of the crowd the proconsul told him to swear by Caesar and curse Christ. His answer has been repeated for almost 1,900 years:

"Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He hath done me no wrong. How can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?"

The story comes from the letter the church at Smyrna wrote after his death, the oldest account of a Christian martyr outside the Bible. Based on true events. Some details come from church accounts.
